skills/toil/jira.md

Issues, JQL search, transitions, comments, worklogs, labels, links, attachments, custom fields, boards and sprints on Jira Data Center / Server (/rest/api/2 and /rest/agile/1.0). Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: Jira Data Center 8.14 or later (REST API 2 and Agile REST API 1.0). toil authenticates with a personal access token, which Jira Data Center added in 8.14. No release has been verified yet.

Credential

A Jira personal access token: in Jira, your profile picture → Profile → Personal Access Tokens → Create token. toil sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. There is no username, password or browser login.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_JIRA_BASE_URLyesJira server root, e.g. https://jira.imagile.dev (keep any context path, e.g. https://jira.imagile.dev/jira)
apiTokenTOIL_JIRA_API_TOKENyesPersonal access token
customFieldsTOIL_JIRA_CUSTOM_FIELDS (JSON)noCustom fields addressable by friendly name; see Custom fields
projectTOIL_JIRA_PROJECTnoDefault project for create-issue
issueTypeTOIL_JIRA_ISSUE_TYPEnoDefault issue type for create-issue (Task when unset)
priorityTOIL_JIRA_PRIORITYnoDefault priority for create-issue
writesTOIL_JIRA_WRITESnotrue lets write commands run (with --allow-write)

Environment variables (CI, or a one-off shell):

export TOIL_JIRA_BASE_URL=https://jira.imagile.dev
export TOIL_JIRA_API_TOKEN=<your personal access token>

Or ~/.toil/config.json, with project, issueType and priority usually set once under defaults.jira so every Jira connection shares them:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "corp-jira": { "area": "jira", "baseUrl": "https://jira.imagile.dev", "writes": true }
  },
  "defaults": { "jira": { "connection": "corp-jira", "project": "ABC", "issueType": "Story" } }
}

The token never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add corp-jira --area jira (or toil connections login corp-jira for an existing connection) to keep it in the OS credential store, which writes "apiToken": "keychain:…", or set TOIL_JIRA_API_TOKEN.

Env vars always win over the file. A second Jira server is a second connection ("lab-jira": { "area": "jira", ... }), chosen per call with --connection lab-jira or configured from env with TOIL_CONN_LAB_JIRA_AREA=jira plus TOIL_CONN_LAB_JIRA_BASE_URL and TOIL_CONN_LAB_JIRA_API_TOKEN.

Commands

Every command also takes --connection <name>. Write commands (marked ✎) need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write; over MCP they are only listed when writes are on, and allowWrite: true stands in for the flag.

CommandFlagsReturns
get-issue--keyThe issue; registered custom fields under their friendly names
create-issue ✎--project --type --summary --description --priority --assignee --labels --parent --field (repeatable) --fields-file --input-fileThe created issue, read back
update-issue ✎--key --summary --description --priority --assignee --labels --field --fields-file --input-file{ updated }
schema--example-only{ schema, example } for --input-file, or just the example
transition-issue ✎--key --transition <name-or-id>{ transitioned, transition }
list-transitions--keyTransitions available now
add-comment ✎--key --bodyThe comment
list-comments--keyEvery comment
log-work ✎--key --time-spent --comment --startedThe worklog
search--jql or --jql-file, --max-results --start-at --fields{ issues, total, startAt, maxResults }
add-label ✎ / remove-label ✎--key --labels a,b{ updated, labelsAdded } / { updated, labelsRemoved }
assign ✎--key --assignee <username>{ assigned, assignee }
link-issue ✎--key --link-type --target{ linked, to, type }
add-attachment ✎--key --fileThe attachments created
list-attachments--keyAttachments (id, filename, size, mimeType, content)
download-attachment--key --attachment-id --dir{ saved, filename, size }; saves to .toil/ by default
fields--discover --custom-only --project --issue-typeRegistered fields, or Jira’s field list with suggestedType and allowedValues
list-boards--projectBoards (id, name, scrum or kanban)
list-sprints--board or --project, --state active,future,closedSprints with dates and goal
set-sprint ✎--key --sprint <id>{ updated, sprint }
api<method> <path> --query key=value (repeatable) --body-file --content-typeThe response body; see Any endpoint below. ✎ for POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
check-dossier--dossier <name|file> (or the folder’s dossier){ dossier, connection, env, ok, checked, checks, unchecked }: each project and field id the dossier names, found or not; exit 1 when one is missing

Over MCP the same commands are tools named jira_<command> with hyphens as underscores (jira_get_issue, jira_list_sprints), taking camelCase fields (key, issueType, maxResults, attachmentId).

Examples

toil jira get-issue --key ABC-123
toil jira search --jql 'project = ABC AND status = "In Progress"' --max-results 20
toil jira search --jql-file query.jql --fields summary,status,"Story Points"
toil jira create-issue --project ABC --type Bug --summary "Login broken on Safari" --priority High --allow-write
toil jira transition-issue --key ABC-123 --transition "In Progress" --allow-write
toil jira add-comment --key ABC-123 --body "Reproduced on staging." --allow-write
toil jira log-work --key ABC-123 --time-spent "2h 30m" --comment "Investigated the failing build" --allow-write
toil jira list-sprints --project ABC --state active,future
toil jira set-sprint --key ABC-123 --sprint 42 --allow-write
toil jira download-attachment --key ABC-123 --attachment-id 10001 --dir downloads

search without --max-results pages through every match, so bound broad queries. meta.page.nextCursor is the --start-at for the next page (or null). create-issue takes its project from --project, then project in --input-file, then the connection’s project, and meta.context.inputs.project says which: input for the flag or the file, connection for the setting (TOIL_JIRA_PROJECT and defaults.jira.project both report connection, not default). The --project on fields, list-boards and list-sprints never falls back to the connection. --time-spent takes Jira durations (1d, 2h 30m); --started takes Jira’s datetime format (2024-01-15T09:00:00.000+0000) and defaults to now.

Any endpoint: jira api

When no command above covers an endpoint, jira api calls it directly. It sends the connection’s own credential, the same way every other jira command does, to a path under the connection’s baseUrl:

toil jira api GET /rest/api/2/myself
toil jira api GET /rest/api/2/issue/ABC-123/changelog --query maxResults=50
toil jira api GET /rest/agile/1.0/board/12/backlog --query fields=summary --query maxResults=20
toil jira api POST /rest/api/2/version --body-file version.json --allow-write
toil jira api PUT /rest/api/2/issue/ABC-123/watchers --body-file user.json --content-type application/json --allow-write
  • The path is relative to baseUrl (a context path such as /jira is kept), with or without a leading / (in Git Bash on Windows, leave it off: the shell rewrites /rest/... into a file path, which is refused). A full URL, a scheme, //host, a leading backslash or a . / .. segment is refused with INVALID_INPUT before anything is sent, so the token never leaves the connection’s host.
  • The method decides the gate. GET and HEAD are reads. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are writes: they need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write. DELETE works only on the CLI: over MCP, jira_api refuses it with INVALID_INPUT.
  • --query key=value adds a query parameter; repeat it for more, or to repeat a key. --body-file <path> sends that file (inside the workspace, or - for stdin) as the body, as application/json unless --content-type says otherwise.
  • Output: a JSON body is data, parsed. A text body (text/*, XML, or no content type) is data as text. Any other body is binary: data is its bytes as base64, with an API_BINARY warning (use download-attachment to save an attachment). Text and binary are capped at 1 MB, with an API_TRUNCATED warning when the body was longer. An empty body (a 204, a HEAD) is null. meta.response is { status, contentType }. Errors use the usual codes (AUTH, NOT_FOUND, HTTP, NETWORK) with Jira’s own message. A body labelled JSON that doesn’t parse comes back as text, with an API_NOT_JSON warning.
  • Over MCP it’s the jira_api tool, with method, path, query (an array of key=value strings), bodyFile, contentType and allowWrite.

Prefer a wrapped command when one exists: it knows the endpoint’s paging, custom fields and quirks, and jira api doesn’t.

Large fields via —input-file

create-issue and update-issue take --input-file <path> (- reads stdin on the CLI) describing the issue as { project, issueType, fields: { ... } }. toil jira schema returns its JSON Schema and an example. Any string value in fields may be @path/to/file to read it from a file. Flags override matching keys from the file, and each override is reported in meta.warnings.

toil jira schema --example-only > envelope.json   # the example is in .data
toil jira create-issue --input-file issue.json --priority Low --allow-write

Over MCP, - is refused because stdin carries the protocol; pass a file path. Relative paths resolve against the directory toil runs in.

Custom fields

--field Name=value (repeatable), --fields-file and --input-file accept a raw field id (customfield_10032) or a standard field name (fixVersions) with no setup. Name=@file.json reads the value from a file: JSON when it parses, text otherwise, which also avoids shell quoting trouble in PowerShell.

To use a friendly name in flags, JQL and output, register the field on the connection:

"customFields": [{ "id": "customfield_10016", "name": "Story Points", "type": "number" }]

type shapes a --field value: string, number, date, datetime, select ({value}), multi-select, option-id ({id}), cascading-select (parent or parent:child ids), user ({name}), labels, url, textarea. Omit it to send the raw string. toil jira fields --discover lists Jira’s fields with a suggestedType; add --project ABC to see each select field’s allowedValues. A select field that only accepts option ids needs "type": "option-id". Sprint is not a custom field: use set-sprint after the issue exists.

A dossier can name fields too ("jira": { "fields": { "storyPoints": "customfield_10016" } }, or toil dossiers field <dossier> jira storyPoints customfield_10016). Then create-issue and update-issue take --field storyPoints=5 in any folder the dossier applies to. An alias takes the type the connection registers for that id. A name the connection already uses keeps the connection’s meaning.

Data Center, not Cloud

This area targets Jira Data Center and Server. Users are usernames (--assignee jsmith, user-typed fields send { "name": ... }), where Jira Cloud needs an accountId. Jira Cloud is a separate area, jira-cloud, with its own TOIL_JIRA_CLOUD_* settings; don’t point this one at a Cloud site.

Notes

  • create-issue doesn’t check for duplicates. After a timeout, search for the summary before retrying: the issue may already exist.
  • update-issue with nothing to change still sends an empty update and reports { updated }.
  • download-attachment never replaces a file. If one of the same name is already in the target directory, it fails with INVALID_INPUT; delete the file or pass a different --dir.
  • download-attachment only ever sends the token to baseUrl’s host. If Jira names another host for the file, toil fetches the same path from baseUrl and warns.

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Jira server root, e.g. https://jira.imagile.dev

    TOIL_JIRA_BASE_URL

  • apiToken required secret

    Personal access token

    TOIL_JIRA_API_TOKEN

  • customFields

    Custom fields addressable by friendly name

    TOIL_JIRA_CUSTOM_FIELDS

  • project

    Default project key for create-issue

    TOIL_JIRA_PROJECT

  • issueType

    Default issue type for create-issue (Task when unset)

    TOIL_JIRA_ISSUE_TYPE

  • priority

    Default priority for create-issue

    TOIL_JIRA_PRIORITY

Commands at a glance

  • toil jiraget-issue

    Get a Jira issue by key

    MCP jira_get_issue--key <issue-key>

  • toil jiracreate-issuewrite

    Create a Jira issue

    MCP jira_create_issue--type <type>--summary <text>--description <text>--priority <name>--assignee <username>--labels <labels>--parent <key>--field <Name=value>--fields-file <path>--input-file <path>--project <key>--allow-write

  • toil jiraupdate-issuewrite

    Update a Jira issue

    MCP jira_update_issue--key <issue-key>--summary <text>--description <text>--priority <name>--assignee <username>--labels <labels>--field <Name=value>--fields-file <path>--input-file <path>--allow-write

  • toil jiraschema

    Print the --input-file JSON schema and an example for create-issue/update-issue

    MCP jira_schema--example-only

  • toil jiratransition-issuewrite

    Transition a Jira issue to a new status

    MCP jira_transition_issue--key <issue-key>--transition <name-or-id>--allow-write

  • toil jiralist-transitions

    List available transitions for an issue

    MCP jira_list_transitions--key <issue-key>

  • toil jiraadd-commentwrite

    Add a comment to a Jira issue

    MCP jira_add_comment--key <issue-key>--body <text>--allow-write

  • toil jiralog-workwrite

    Add a worklog (time spent) entry to a Jira issue

    MCP jira_log_work--key <issue-key>--time-spent <duration>--comment <text>--started <datetime>--allow-write

  • toil jiralist-comments

    List comments on a Jira issue

    MCP jira_list_comments--key <issue-key>

  • toil jiraadd-labelwrite

    Add one or more labels to a Jira issue (non-destructive)

    MCP jira_add_label--key <issue-key>--labels <labels>--allow-write

  • toil jiraremove-labelwrite

    Remove one or more labels from a Jira issue (non-destructive)

    MCP jira_remove_label--key <issue-key>--labels <labels>--allow-write

  • toil jiraassignwrite

    Assign a Jira issue to a user

    MCP jira_assign--key <issue-key>--assignee <username>--allow-write

  • toil jiralink-issuewrite

    Link two Jira issues together

    MCP jira_link_issue--key <issue-key>--link-type <type>--target <issue-key>--allow-write

  • toil jirasearch

    Search Jira issues with JQL (consider --output-file for large results)

    MCP jira_search--jql <query>--jql-file <path>--max-results <n>--start-at <n>--fields <list>

  • toil jirafields

    List custom fields (configured or discovered from Jira API) (consider --output-file for large results)

    MCP jira_fields--discover--custom-only--project <key>--issue-type <type>

  • toil jiraadd-attachmentwrite

    Upload a file as an attachment to a Jira issue

    MCP jira_add_attachment--key <issue-key>--file <path>--allow-write

  • toil jiralist-attachments

    List attachments on a Jira issue

    MCP jira_list_attachments--key <issue-key>

  • toil jiradownload-attachment

    Download a Jira issue attachment to .toil/ (or --dir)

    MCP jira_download_attachment--key <issue-key>--attachment-id <id>--dir <path>

  • toil jiralist-boards

    List Agile boards for a project

    MCP jira_list_boards--project <key>

  • toil jiralist-sprints

    List sprints for a board or project, including start/end dates

    MCP jira_list_sprints--board <id>--project <key>--state <states>

  • toil jiraset-sprintwrite

    Move a Jira issue into a sprint

    MCP jira_set_sprint--key <issue-key>--sprint <id>--allow-write

  • toil jiraapiwrite

    Call any Jira Data Center REST endpoint on the connection, e.g. toil jira api GET /rest/api/2/issue/PAY-1042

    MCP jira_api<method><path>--query <key=value>--body-file <path>--content-type <type>--allow-write

  • toil jiracheck-dossier

    Check the call's dossier against Jira: its projects and field ids exist

    MCP jira_check_dossier
